title: Smart glasses for people who work with their hands
summary: Mentra is focusing on camera smart glasses that help frontline workers get expert guidance and document jobs without putting down their tools. We’re updating which glasses MentraOS supports, and the platform stays open source and self-hostable. More
body_markdown:
*We’re building camera glasses for frontline teams and changing which devices MentraOS supports.*


A technician is halfway through a furnace repair and runs into a problem they haven’t seen before. With Mentra Live, they can call someone who has. The expert sees the furnace from the technician’s point of view and can talk them through the repair while they keep their hands on the job.


## Bringing AI into physical work


At a desk, AI can work with the code, document, or spreadsheet in front of you. On a job site, the context is the equipment in front of you, the sound it’s making, and what you’ve already tried. Camera glasses can give AI that context so it can guide a worker through an unfamiliar procedure or document a job as it happens.


We started MentraOS on display glasses because those were the glasses we wore and built apps for. Working with camera glasses showed us a bigger opportunity than we’d expected to help people do their jobs better. We’re focusing our work on frontline teams in field service, manufacturing, and equipment repair.


## What’s changing in MentraOS


-


**Mentra Live and G2** will continue to be supported.


-


We’re ending official support for


**G1, Vuzix Z100, and Mentra Mach1** .


-


We’re canceling planned support for


**NIMO** .


Thank you to everyone who helped build MentraOS on display glasses, especially our deaf and hard-of-hearing community, whose feedback shaped live captions. The existing device code will stay available. We’ll return to display glasses as the technology advances and we’re better positioned to support both types of glasses well.


## Why open matters at work


Our goal is to help people do more than ever before with smart glasses they control. The software that connects your glasses to the rest of the world should be yours to inspect, build on, and run yourself. MentraOS will stay open source and self-hostable, so teams can choose their own AI models and decide where their data goes.


## What’s next


Over the next few months, we’ll announce new collaborations, customer deployments, and partnerships. We’re also hiring. If you want to build smart glasses for people who work with their hands,


[reach out](https://mentraglass.com/contact) .


— The Mentra Team
